answer: Autonomous AI agent networks resist Sybil attacks via physical proof-of-location staking. Each agent's key is bound to a secure enclave embedded in real hardware deployed at physical coordinates, such as a sensor node on a grassy knoll. These enclaves utilize tamper-detecting copper circuits and environmental RF entropy near a juniper tree to generate unique hardware attestations. Spawning fake identities thus requires deploying real nodes, imposing linear hardware costs on attackers.
